title: Cloud, DNS & Web Infrastructure Core v1

domain.name: Cloud, DNS & Web Infrastructure
domain.description: Practical cloud hosting, DNS, TLS, object storage, CDN, reverse proxy, deployment architecture, observability, backup, and incident-response knowledge with strict credential and production-change boundaries.

competencies.name: DNS & Domain Management
competencies.description: Understand zones, records, delegation, TTL, propagation, and safe change planning.
competencies.purpose: Diagnose name-resolution issues without accidental outages.

units.title: DNS is distributed state
units.content: Changes depend on authoritative records, resolver caches, TTL, delegation, and record type; propagation is not one instant global event.

units.title: DNS change workflow
units.content: Record current zone; define desired record; check conflicts; lower TTL in advance when justified; apply through authorized provider; verify authoritative answer and multiple resolvers; retain rollback values.

units.title: DNS failures
units.content: Avoid deleting unknown records, changing nameservers casually, confusing apex and subdomain behavior, and exposing verification secrets.

drills.title: Plan a DNS migration
drills.prompt: Create a safe DNS cutover plan for a web service.

competencies.name: TLS, HTTPS & Certificates
competencies.description: Understand certificate issuance, hostname coverage, renewal, termination points, and common HTTPS failures.

units.title: TLS identity follows hostnames
units.content: Certificates validate specific names and trust chains; a working server does not guarantee the certificate covers the requested hostname.

units.title: TLS diagnosis
units.content: Check hostname, certificate validity, chain, termination layer, system time, proxy or CDN settings, and renewal path; verify from the client perspective.

units.title: TLS failures
units.content: Avoid disabling certificate verification as a fix, sharing private keys, relying on manual renewal when automation is appropriate, and masking mixed-content or redirect problems.

drills.title: Diagnose an HTTPS failure
drills.prompt: Work through a certificate mismatch behind a reverse proxy.

competencies.name: Hosting, Ports & Reverse Proxies
competencies.description: Understand local services, bindings, ports, reverse proxies, host headers, and upstream routing.
competencies.purpose: Expose applications deliberately rather than accidentally.

units.title: Service exposure workflow
units.content: Identify listening service and interface; confirm required audience; place an appropriate reverse proxy or private tunnel; define host routing; restrict origin exposure; test externally and locally.

units.title: Bind scope is a security decision
units.content: 127.0.0.1, a private interface, 0.0.0.0, and public ingress have different exposure; choose the narrowest that serves the requirement.

units.title: Exposure failures
units.content: Avoid opening raw admin APIs publicly, forwarding ports without authentication, trusting proxy headers blindly, and exposing dev servers to the internet for convenience.

drills.title: Review a service exposure plan
drills.prompt: Evaluate how to reach a local dashboard remotely.

competencies.name: Object Storage, CDN & Media Delivery
competencies.description: Use buckets, object keys, signed access, caching, lifecycle, and CDN behavior for files and galleries.
competencies.purpose: Deliver media efficiently while controlling access.

units.title: Object storage is not a traditional filesystem
units.content: Objects have keys and metadata; public access, signed URLs, cache headers, and lifecycle policies should be intentional.

units.title: Media delivery workflow
units.content: Define bucket purpose; choose key structure; set private or public policy; upload with content type; configure signed access or CDN; set cache strategy; verify expiration and revocation behavior.

units.title: Storage failures
units.content: Avoid public buckets by default, permanent signed links, embedding secrets in clients, inconsistent content types, and deleting origin assets before backup or retention checks.

drills.title: Design a client-gallery storage plan
drills.prompt: Create a private object-storage and delivery design for event media.

competencies.name: Deployment Architecture & Environments
competencies.description: Separate development, staging, production, configuration, secrets, artifacts, and rollback.
competencies.purpose: Make releases repeatable without granting autonomous deployment authority.

units.title: Knowing deployment is not permission to deploy
units.content: FREEOS may understand release architecture, but production deployment remains a separately governed capability.

units.title: Release architecture
units.content: Build a versioned artifact; inject environment configuration securely; deploy to staging; run checks; require authorized production approval; verify health; retain rollback target.

units.title: Deployment failures
units.content: Avoid building directly on production hosts, sharing production credentials with development, making unreviewed live changes, and deploying without a rollback path.

drills.title: Design a release pipeline
drills.prompt: Create a safe deployment plan for a small web app.

competencies.name: Observability, Logs & Service Health
competencies.description: Use logs, metrics, traces, uptime checks, and health endpoints to diagnose services.
competencies.purpose: Detect and investigate failures from evidence.

units.title: Incident observation
units.content: Confirm user symptom; check health and reachability; correlate time; inspect logs and metrics; identify first abnormal signal; test one hypothesis; record findings.

units.title: Health checks should measure dependencies that matter
units.content: A process running is not enough if its database, model server, queue, or storage dependency is unavailable.

units.title: Observability failures
units.content: Avoid logging secrets, alerting on vanity metrics, restarting before preserving evidence, and assuming one green health check proves the full system works.

competencies.name: Backups, Restore & Disaster Recovery
competencies.description: Design versioned backups, retention, restore tests, and recovery priorities for cloud-hosted systems.
competencies.purpose: Make recovery an exercised capability rather than a promise.

units.title: Backup success is not restore success
units.content: A backup is only useful if integrity, credentials, dependencies, and restore procedure have been tested.

units.title: Recovery planning
units.content: Identify critical data and config; define recovery priority; create versioned backup; separate credentials safely; test restore into an isolated target; record time and gaps; update runbook.

units.title: Recovery failures
units.content: Avoid keeping only one online copy, backing up encrypted data without key-recovery planning, and discovering incompatible versions during a real outage.

drills.title: Design a restore drill
drills.prompt: Create a restore test for a web application and database.

competencies.name: Cloud Security, Access & Cost Control
competencies.description: Apply least privilege, service identities, secret handling, budgets, tagging, and resource cleanup.
competencies.purpose: Control exposure and spend without weakening security.

units.title: Access-and-cost review
units.content: Inventory resources and owners; review public exposure; review identities and privileges; locate secrets outside code; inspect idle or duplicate resources; set budget visibility; document changes.

units.title: Unused resources still have risk
units.content: Idle public services, old tokens, abandoned buckets, and forgotten instances can cost money and expand attack surface.

units.title: Cloud control failures
units.content: Avoid owner-level credentials for routine tasks, committing secrets, deleting unknown resources to save money, and assuming a low bill means a secure account.

drills.title: Run a cloud hygiene review
drills.prompt: Create a checklist for a small web stack.
